column6: The back-translated paragraph maintains the same conceptual meaning as the original, conveying the experience of a profound communication with the Lord while acknowledging uncertainty about the nature of that communication.
column7: There was one time when His Word came so clear and bold that it could have been audible. I answered Him by speaking out, it was so real. However, there was no one there but the Lord and I, so I can’t really say for sure if He spoke to me like we speak to each other.
column8: There was a time when His word came so clearly and vividly that it might as well have been audible. I answered Him out loud because it was that real. However, there was no one there but the Lord and me, so I cannot say with certainty whether He spoke to me as in a conversational exchange between us.

column6: Both paragraphs convey the same core idea that true understanding is not derived from logical reasoning but is instead a complete thought or perception. The wording has changed slightly, but the underlying meaning remains consistent.
column7: 2.  <u>The KNOWING is NOT built by logic within your mind; however, it is a complete thought or understanding.</u>
column8: 2.  <u>This inner knowing is not formed by the reasoning of your mind; rather, it is a complete thought or perception.</u>

column6: The original paragraph emphasizes that God does not convict (implying a sense of guilt or punishment) but convinces (suggesting persuasion towards truth). The back-translation changes 'convicts' to 'condemns' and 'convinces' to 'assures,' altering the theological implications of God's communication with His children.
column7: 5.  <u>When He speaks to His children, He NEVER CONVICTS; He CONVINCES.</u>
column8: 5.  <u>When He speaks to His children, He never condemns; He assures.</u>

column6: The back-translation introduces terms like 'belittle' and 'evil and despair,' which shift the focus from the original's emphasis on 'running down' and 'doom and gloom.' This alters the doctrinal implications regarding God's nature and the messages He conveys, suggesting a more negative connotation.
column7: God never takes you down! He will never run you down; He only builds you up. When God speaks to you, He is speaking from the frame of reference that everything the Word says about you has already been accomplished and ACCEPTED by you. Jeremiah 33:3 says: “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you **GREAT AND MIGHTY** things which you do not know.” Does that sound like running you down or doom and gloom? There is NO doom and gloom in God, therefore He cannot tell you anything doomy or gloomy. You’ll have to tune in to the world’s news agency for doom and gloom.
column8: God will never put you down! He will never belittle you; He only builds you up. When God speaks with you, He speaks from a perspective that what the Word says about you is already accomplished and you have received it. Jeremiah 33:3 says: “Call to Me, and I will answer you, and show you great and mighty things, which you do not know.” Does that sound like putting you down or like evil and despair? There is no evil or despair in God; therefore He cannot speak to you any message of pessimism or gloom. For evil and despair you will have to pay attention to the world’s news agencies.
